approach.method_basis: The Parent is a molecular graph evolutionary search guided by a session-local Gaussian process. It keeps all real accepted scores for the predictor and the best sixty-four scored molecules for breeding. Score-quantile parent selection, connected-fragment crossover with optional finishing edits, and short one-, two- or three-call mutation chains create a fresh pool of 160 graphs for each announced batch. Canonical identity, duplicate, size and source-relative sulfur checks control admission. A Gaussian process uses raw chiral Morgan environment counts and the dot-product Tanimoto kernel, with the accepted-score mean and scale and a fixed observation-noise level. After three consecutive batches without an incumbent improvement, only the forty highest original posterior means remain eligible; the full pool returns on the first improving batch. For each purchase position the Parent draws a separate function row with correlation across candidates and selects its largest eligible, not-yet-selected value. Only actual returned scores update the archive, survivors and breeding state.
approach.novelty: Replace that last purchase rule by GIBBON maximum-information allocation. Joint latent draws over the current generated pool and already accepted inputs estimate a reachable maximum; each candidate receives an information-quality term, and the batch pays for redundancy through its noisy predictive correlation. Greedy filling combines those two terms without invented feedback. This differs from same-Parent attempts that changed predictive location, response likelihood, covariance models, residual use or winner-event frequency: the new criterion values information about the maximum. It also differs from the earlier determinant sampler, which reweighted posterior winners without this maximum-value information quality. The test is whether the changed purchases feed useful later search under the unchanged generator, then improve the final observed endpoint.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is the conversion of the retained GP into useful later purchases, rather than a demonstrated inability to fit accepted scores. The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de completes every Search cell at mean 0.607030316211131 (seed SD 0.030175277546149237), yet its existing analysis reports late concentration on substituted families and only 253 incumbent improvements among 4350 optimizer purchases. A fresh read-only audit of every Parent log/trajectory gives equal-session positive generating-parent gain per paid molecule 0.0038830439945360625 over all 4350 purchases and 0.0020240780825076187 over all 2175 optimizer ordinals 146..290. It verifies 435 complete 160-member fields, 88 restricted allocations, all 15 chronological score/provenance joins and no fallback. See policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/parent-evidence.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files, which cite and hash the underlying log, trajectory, summary and run files. The frozen review's control n-61cb8ba305fa gains 0.041860730188559035 over its weighted code Parent while its passive mixture has lower paid-stream MSE than the active GP (0.01098210970157113 versus 0.011599451325391918). The preserved policy/scratch/round75-search-policy/evidence-review.json and all fifteen indexed audit-seed-N-task.json files establish that this control restores exactly the formal Anchor trajectories; those are dependent evidence, not extra replications or a new improvement. The specific contrary variants remain scoped: n-9b90d71cc6e1 on the earlier mask-free Parent lowered count similarity 0.6660 to 0.5798 but lowered endpoints by 0.038159276809506; n-698a02f85be1 on the stall-mask Parent correctly executed calibrated EI with mean-fantasy conditioning yet lost 0.05328817319169632; n-9002c3d22369 learned noise under a binary-feature host, improved selected-stream MSE, and lost 0.01596063945276797. These observations motivate testing maximum information with both quality and noisy redundancy; none establishes that the new criterion will help, or refutes every information acquisition rule.

adoptions.applicability: n-61cb8ba305fa demonstrates that lower squared error can be a poor purchase objective. Historical c-f0e8bd37b9 and n-9002c3d22369 show that this disconnect predates the pair learner. n-9b90d71cc6e1 already diversified batches but lost quality and endpoints, and n-698a02f85be1 exercised immediate improvement pricing without gain. GIBBON uses a different quantity: information about the maximum with model-derived redundancy and quality together, not determinant repulsion alone.

method_change.previous_method: Final sequential masked maxima of separate correlated GP posterior function rows over the fresh eligible graph pool on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de.
method_change.proposed_method: Final greedy GIBBON maximum-information allocation on the same eligible pool, with 128 joint latent maximum samples on fresh-plus-accepted support and noisy predictive correlation redundancy.
method_change.rationale: The actual Parent's late productive gain is limited despite useful ranking, and complete indexed calibration, determinant-diversification and immediate-improvement variants show that their measured proxies need not convert to useful endpoint gains. This one replacement tests whether purchases targeted at a reachable maximum's information improve later real search while preserving the existing predictor and graph host.

hypothesis: One component replacement on actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de: replace only final per-position sampled maxima with finite-support greedy GIBBON. Fit the unchanged accepted-only raw-count T_DP GP once per real announcement, generate the unchanged fresh 160-member pool, and freeze the original K3/M40 eligible set E. Define the maximum support U as every fresh pool graph in generation order followed by every real accepted input in archive order. Using the same conditioned latent GP, draw exactly 128 joint latent function rows on U from a separate reproducible generator and take each row's maximum m_r. Accepted inputs are uncertain latent representers conditioned on their real labels, never repurchasable candidates or score clamps. Exact count-vector aliases share one latent variable. No Gumbel fit, clipping of maxima, task-based bound or external support enters. For an eligible candidate i let mu_i be its original raw-unit predictive mean, s_i its original latent SD, tau=score_scale*0.05, v_i=s_i^2+tau^2, rho_i^2=s_i^2/v_i, gamma_ri=(m_r-mu_i)/s_i and h=phi(gamma_ri)/Phi(gamma_ri). Compute q_i=-mean_r(log(1-rho_i^2*h*(gamma_ri+h)))/2, with q_i=0 at exactly zero latent variance. Form noisy predictive correlation R from score_scale^2*C_pool+tau^2*I, excluding numerical pool sampling jitter. The registered batch objective is F(B)=sum(i in B) q_i+0.5*logdet(R_B). Starting from empty B, fill every announced position by the largest q_i+0.5*log(1-R_iB*R_BB^(-1)*R_Bi) among E minus B, using Cholesky solves and ascending original pool index for exact ties. The first redundancy increment is zero. Continue unique fill even if all remaining increments are negative; neither clip increments nor change batch size. Quality values and model conditioning stay fixed within this announcement. The Schur complement prices redundancy; it does not insert a fantasy observation. Consume the Parent's original-shaped normal tensor and original pool factor once on its original RNG stream and preserve the original masked TS batch as a passive record only. GIBBON's maximum stream does not consume that RNG or the graph RNG. Only the GIBBON identities are purchased; ordinary accepted feedback then changes the real GP and breeding state. The causal prediction is that this different information allocation changes paid identities and increases the equal-session late positive generating-parent gain per paid molecule after earlier acquired labels enter subsequent fits. Endpoint gain is a separate claim.

finding_summary.headline: GIBBON buys different batches and raises its information bound, but late productive gain and endpoint scores fall
finding_summary.insights:
This is a complete counterexample to the fixed claim that this reachable-maximum information allocation produces more useful later search. The borrowed GIBBON quality and noisy-correlation terms both operated, and earlier purchases actually changed later posterior predictions and remained available for breeding. Thus missing execution, wrong random-stream consumption and absent feedback are ruled out here. Increasing the model's information bound is insufficient to increase positive parent gain or the observed-best endpoint. The model bound is neither measured true information nor a maximum over chemical space: the literature adaptation uses 128 joint samples over the current fresh pool plus accepted inputs, the retained GP noise and inherited eligibility gate. Its finite support, model assumptions, greedy construction and fixed budget limit the inference; this result does not end the information-acquisition approach.

The trajectories separate a purchase-criterion limitation from a universal shortage of scaffold novelty. GIBBON buys less similar batches than passive Thompson on the same state (mean count similarity 0.6396 versus 0.6902), yet the molecular assessment finds 228 very small products across the complete panel versus 98 for the Parent. In the task with the largest endpoint loss, the high-score output narrows to 10 scaffolds versus 21, underrepresents the Parent's more saturated nitrogen-ring and amine alternatives, and spends 117 purchases on products of at most six heavy atoms versus 20. Other tasks reach broader scaffold sets, so global scaffold collapse would be the wrong diagnosis. The observed limitation is that information-directed selection within this inherited graph host can still reward fragment detours or repeatedly decorated families without reaching the more productive alternatives. A proposal operator that preserves connected molecular architecture while exposing alternative ring/linker families, or an allocation model tied to realized downstream improvement, could address that kind of limitation; neither is tested by this node. These chemical associations do not identify which descriptor caused the loss.

The selected-stream GP error is also lower (MSE 0.007148 versus 0.011599), despite lower useful gain; the streams contain different molecules, so this is not a controlled predictor-accuracy improvement. Likewise, 2,491 purchased molecules are later used as parents and the full run records 257 incumbent improvements versus 253 for the Parent, but those counts do not imply a better endpoint. The evidence prices the complete GIBBON allocation replacement negatively under this matched composition. It does not separate the quality term, redundancy term, maximum support, inherited eligibility gate or chemical mediation, and it supplies no counterfactual scores for passive purchases.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 allocations executed correctly with no fallback. Their 55,680 joint maximum samples and all 563,625 available greedy increments reconstruct from the unchanged accepted-only GP. Every purchased batch differed from its same-state passive Thompson batch: 2,790 of 4,350 paid identities changed, with 4,102 positions changed. The average modeled information bound rose from 0.25448 for passive Thompson choices to 0.54936 for GIBBON choices; its quality term rose from 0.44911 to 0.59842 and its redundancy penalty became less negative, from -0.19463 to -0.04906. This establishes the intended information-allocation computation and routing change. All 4,350 purchases join to real feedback; all 4,200 with another announcement enter the next GP fit, with the final 150 correctly censored.

The registered useful-search prediction nevertheless fails. Over exactly the last 145 purchases of each of the 15 sessions, positive gain over the best generating parent averages 0.00174426 per purchase, down from 0.00202408. Twelve of fifteen paired late cells decline and three improve. Early gain also falls, from 0.00574201 to 0.00530950; full-period gain falls from 0.00388304 to 0.00352688. Late parent beaters fall from 238 to 222 out of 2,175 purchases. All three endpoint seed averages decline: -0.10358, -0.02712 and -0.04632. Mean endpoint score is 0.54802 versus 0.60703, a loss of 0.05901, below the required +0.002 improvement. Six task/seed endpoints improve and nine decline. Seed dispersion is smaller, 0.00758 versus 0.03018, around that lower mean. The protocol task-safety test fails on sitagliptin, whose mean endpoint falls by 0.22141; the large decoration-hopping mean loss remains visible but does not pass that test's paired-error requirement. All fifteen tasks completed their 300 accepted observations with zero invalid or duplicate evaluator proposals.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl heterocycles, amines and lactams, with frequent N-halogenation, undefined stereochemistry and small-fragment detours.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment concerns n-294ad2ffe1d4 and its published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de. The frozen comparison independently marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete, both on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All fifteen trusted Child trajectories and fifteen published Parent trajectories were present and read; there are no absent task comparisons. Each side contains 4,350 accepted optimizer products, separate from 150 supplied initial records. The scope is accepted output, not unseen generated pools or rejected proposals. The digest supports abundant rings and aromaticity: task-level ring-closure text rates span 0.8621 to 0.9759, and aromatic-atom text presence rates span 0.8563 to 0.9690. These rates measure molecule-level text presence, not aromatic atom fractions. Actual products include indole-like carboxamides, N-rich fused carbonyl/imine heterocycles, aryl-linked saturated amines, and elaborate fused or bridged lactams. They are neither ring-poor nor globally devoid of basic-amine-like motifs. At the same time, 1,149 products contain N-halogen bonds, 168 contain O-O bonds, and 228 have at most six heavy atoms. No product specifies tetrahedral configuration or formal charge; RDKit perceives unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,579 products. Neutral SMILES do not imply absence of ionisable centres. All these are structural readings, not experimental stability, pKa, synthesis, or biological measurements. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because familiar medicinal fragments coexist with N-halogenation, nitroso variants, cumulene-bearing cages and complicated ring closures. Structural diversity is moderate overall: many skeletons occur, but several high-score families remain close analogues. For reproducibility, full means all 290 optimizer rows per session and late means ordinals 146 through 290, giving 145 rows per session; the pooled high and low deciles each contain 87 molecules per task, with score ties resolved by seed and evaluation order. All sizes, ring counts and scaffolds below were perceived with RDKit 2023.09.6. Source overlap means exact Murcko scaffold matching or maximum radius-two chiral Morgan count T_DP to the ten supplied initial structures; it is not a parentage claim. Scaffold counts include the empty scaffold of acyclic products. The audit SMARTS named cumulated_double_bonds is a broad formal two-double-bond pattern that also matches O=S=O; it is not used here as a reactivity count. The digest and explicit carbon-centred structures support the cumulene discussion. Parent comparisons describe associated output differences under the frozen panel; they establish neither component attribution nor mechanism activation. Frozen request source: policy/requests/r0075-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-a93296fd5309405d.json. Per-task text cites every derived audit and underlying trajectory. Child copies preserve the bytes and hashes of the request-authorized staging files; the copies do not expand SMILES citation authority.

per_task.generated_character: Most products retain an indole-like fused aromatic core connected through a carboxamide or thiocarboxamide to an aryl ring, with methoxy, methyl, vinyl, methylthio or amino substitutions. The pooled full set spans 1 to 42 heavy atoms with median 26; late products span 1 to 32 with the same median. Mean ring counts are 2.885 full and 2.970 late. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 142 is a 24-heavy-atom, three-ring vinyl/methoxy/methyl indole carboxamide whose amide nitrogen bears Br. Seed 0 instead reaches a seven-membered imine-containing fused system with a thiocarbonyl and N-F/N-Br bonds; seed 2 retains an N-halogenated indole/carboxamide with methoxy and methylthio decoration. These are recognizable scaffold families with chemically concerning modifications. The Child has 214 full and 134 late Murcko scaffolds, versus Parent 187 and 94. Mean initial-structure count similarity is 0.606 full and 0.560 late, versus Parent 0.628 and 0.602; exact initial-scaffold matches are 288/870 full and 140/435 late. The dominant indole-anilide scaffold accounts for 50 of the high 87. Parent full/late heavy-atom medians are both 25; this is related chemistry with somewhat different size and ring editing, not a new chemical class. Sources (each audit followed by its underlying Child copy and published Parent trajectory): policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 500/870 full and 403/435 late products, often directly on amide or heterocyclic nitrogen. The Parent also shows this liability (404/870 full), so it is not unique to this Child.
The low tail includes 31 products with at most six heavy atoms and oversized repeated aromatic units; both fail to preserve the compact high-score architecture.
The seven-membered imine/thiocarbonyl branch and N-halogenated indoles have no demonstrated synthesis or stability; accepted valence is insufficient to establish either.
missing_features: Low-score output often lacks the compact, connected three-ring aromatic/carboxamide arrangement retained by the leaders; simple growth and whole-core duplication do not replace it.
The high-score series does not demonstrate a stable, non-N-halogenated family with the same score level. Stability is a chemistry gap, not a proven missing score term.
The record does not identify an absent target-specific pharmacophore that would resolve the plateau; adding one from the objective name would exceed this evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader scores 0.4484138510190879; the corresponding N-Cl product at evaluation 164 and N-F product at 275 have exactly the same score. Thus these observed halogen exchanges do not resolve the plateau. The supplied methoxy-rich indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. A 41-heavy-atom doubled indole/amide product at seed 2 evaluation 31 scores 1.1778138464910174e-10, while ethene at seed 0 evaluation 273 scores 0.0. The high decile has 23 to 27 heavy atoms, all with three perceived rings; 76/87 contain an amide. In this observed set the gradient favors a compact retained aromatic/carboxamide arrangement over both fragmentation and duplication of whole scaffold units. It does not establish N-halogenation as beneficial chemistry: 85/87 high-decile products contain it and the plateau explicitly tolerates multiple halogens.

per_task.generated_character: The output combines nitrogen-rich aromatic heterocycles with carbonyl/imine groups and increasingly elaborate O/S-linked fused or bridged rings. Full products span 1 to 115 heavy atoms, median 31; late products span 1 to 75, also median 31. Mean perceived ring counts are 5.072 full and 5.184 late, versus Parent 4.177 and 4.136. The seed-2 leader is a 31-heavy-atom, six-ring structure: a fluoropyridine carrying C=C=N decoration and an NH-linked, chlorinated O/S-containing polycycle with aminal and imine centres. It includes a four-membered perceived ring. Seed 0 instead reaches an aminal-linked azaaromatic/carbonyl-imine series with N-halogenation; seed 1 reaches a 40-heavy-atom, six-ring N-rich multiring carbonyl system. This is diverse ring connectivity, with uncertain stereochemistry and synthetic practicality. Child full/late scaffold counts are 434/201 versus Parent 347/138; mean similarity to the supplied initial structures is 0.431/0.381 versus Parent 0.494/0.448. Only 32/870 full and 5/435 late products exactly match an initial Murcko scaffold. Sources (each audit followed by its underlying Child copy and published Parent trajectory): policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0075-02-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl.
liabilities: The digest reports a cumulated-double-bond text rate of 0.0874 and explicitly shows ketenimine-like C=C=N and isocyanate-like N=C=O variants. These warrant chemical reactivity assessment rather than being treated as ordinary stable linkers.

All high 87 contain unassigned tetrahedral centres and aminal carbons. Several chlorinated bridge and O/S ring systems would require geometry, stereochemistry and route checks before synthetic plausibility could be established.
There are 112 O-O-containing products and 29 products with at most six heavy atoms. The high-score set is not evidence that these collateral products are practical molecular designs.
missing_features: Low-score members lack the retained compact N-rich ring/linker arrangements that characterize the high decile; very large scaffold concatenations do not supply them effectively.

The record does not show a stereochemically specified, readily interpretable alternative to the high-score aminal/imine polycycles. It cannot establish that stereochemical specification itself would increase this score.
Different Parent and Child high-score structures prevent a unique absent-group explanation; both carbonyl-rich and imine-rich ring systems appear in the evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 2 evaluation 221 scores 0.6464317070111627. The Br-for-Cl analogue at evaluation 254 has exactly that score, as do several ring-length and O/S variants in the digest. All high 87 have 28 to 34 heavy atoms and contain an imine and an aminal carbon; the high-set ring mean is 5.782. A smaller 20-heavy-atom acylated fused N-heterocycle at seed 0 evaluation 55 scores 0.5193878392871876; the 115-heavy-atom multiscaffold product at seed 1 evaluation 67 scores 0.5776171151648871; ClCl scores 0.5. The observed gradient therefore concerns particular compact N-rich arrangements, rather than monotonic size or ring addition. The published Parent high decile uses a different mixture: all 87 have carbonyls and none has the audit formal-double-bond cumulene pattern, whereas the Child leaders include explicit C=C=N. The Child seed-0 best is 0.616201490047815 versus Parent 0.8561477222467935; this paired difference accompanies different chemotypes, not proof that one functional group caused it.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-score products are aryl-rich molecules with saturated amine linkers or nitrogen rings, including piperazine-like and imidazolidine-like motifs, primary amino side chains, aryl ethers/phenols, halogens and sometimes thiols. The full set spans 1 to 92 heavy atoms, median 31, and the late set 1 to 41, median 31. Full/late mean ring counts are 3.045/3.039, with carbon sp3 fractions 0.403/0.414. liabilities: All high 87 have unassigned tetrahedral centres. Chlorinated aminal carbons, small-ring fusions, aminoalkenes and aryl thiols occur among the leaders; these limit confidence in practical stability and synthesis.
N-halogen bonds occur in 152/870 full products, including some high-score products; 29 accepted products contain at most six heavy atoms.
The score is not a measured binding pose, selectivity, exposure or synthetic feasibility result. The chemical reading establishes motifs and associated scores only.
missing_features: The lowest organic products often lack an accessible unacylated aliphatic amine in the aryl-linked architecture found in the high set. This feature is present elsewhere in this generator, so it is a distribution gap rather than a global inability.

The high-score saturated products do not specify their tetrahedral stereochemistry; no explicit protonation-state comparison is supplied. Charge absence must not be confused with absence of basic nitrogen.
No score-supported absent receptor-specific pharmacophore beyond the observed aryl/amine association can be identified from these records alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 1 evaluation 292 scores 0.9965762739096129 and seed 2 evaluation 264 scores 0.9940283823590779. By contrast, the 20-heavy-atom sulfonylated pyrrolidine/N-chloroamide at seed 2 evaluation 14 scores 0.00016650955053713697; its ring nitrogen is sulfonylated rather than an unacylated aliphatic amine. The high 87 all carry the defined unacylated aliphatic-amine structural proxy, versus 12/87 low members; the Parent high 87 also all carry that proxy. The high set has 25 to 33 heavy atoms and a mean of 12 aromatic atoms. The 92-heavy-atom multiscaffold molecule at seed 1 evaluation 36 scores only 0.02885850823057245. Within these trajectories the association is with medium-sized connected aromatic/amine architectures, not indiscriminate expansion. Seed 0 reaches 0.9867076204574161 while retaining a sulfonamide, so the evidence does not support a rule that sulfonamide removal alone produces the gradient.

per_task.generated_character: These products are carbonyl-rich, N-containing fused or bridged ring systems with aromatic/aza-aromatic components, cyclic amides, ethers and alkyl decoration. Full products span 1 to 62 heavy atoms, median 33; late products span 3 to 49, median 34. Mean ring counts are 4.866 full and 5.057 late, and mean aromatic atom counts 12.500/12.398. The seed-1 leader is a 31-heavy-atom, four-ring conjugated polycycle carrying ethoxy/propyl substituents and an N-methyl lactam segment; RDKit perceives a nine-membered ring in it. Seed 0 instead produces a 37-heavy-atom imine/amide-rich ring system including an eleven-membered ring; seed 2 reaches a 33-heavy-atom N/O-linked fused/bridged lactam system. The Child explores 639 full and 318 late scaffolds, versus Parent 560/277, so broad ring-topology variation is real here. liabilities: The graph constructions include large heterocycles, bridged/fused lactams and ambiguous stereocentres. RDKit ring perception alone does not establish a realizable low-strain geometry or a synthetic route.

Thirty-nine full-set molecules contain a perceived ring of at most four entirely aromatic atoms; none belongs to the high 87. This flags topology to inspect, not a blanket assertion that every such graph is impossible.
Nitroso groups occur in 29 full products and 13 of the high 87, including the cited N-nitroso lactam analogue. High score therefore does not uniformly exclude chemically concerning groups.
missing_features: Lower-score fragments and enlarged concatenations fail to retain the compact combination of aromatic structure and cyclic carbonyl/N linkers seen among the leaders.

The output lacks stereochemically specified versions and demonstrated geometrically practical constructions of its large/fused ring systems; neither missing item is a proven cause of the score ceiling.
Because many scaffold topologies were actually reached, the evidence does not support describing this task as a general lack of scaffold novelty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader at evaluation 275 scores 0.2512109625337072. Its N-nitroso analogue at evaluation 195 scores 0.24679583573735037, so a nearly matching score does not guarantee a desirable functional group. The high 87 have 30 to 36 heavy atoms; all contain carbonyl groups and 84 contain the audit amide motif. A 21-heavy-atom sulfonylated hydroxamate-containing ring product at seed 0 evaluation 19 scores 0.10357020255297016, and the 62-heavy-atom joined multiscaffold product at seed 2 evaluation 17 scores 0.13159540872755981; methane and ethene reach 0.0. The trajectory association favors retaining a combined aromatic/aza-aromatic and cyclic-carbonyl architecture within a medium size range, rather than merely carrying an amide or adding rings. Parent high-decile carbonyl/amide counts are 87/81; its mean aromatic atom count is 10.655 versus Child 15.908. These are alternative observed assemblies, not a uniquely identified missing scaffold.

The seed-1 leader has 25 heavy atoms, three rings, carbonyl-rich fused heterocycles and two N-F attachments. Seed 2 remains in a phenolic N-rich carbonyl/thione family. liabilities: There are 117 products with at most six heavy atoms, including 46 late purchases, versus Parent 20 full and eight late. The size defect remains visible after substantial search.
N-halogen bonds occur in 275/870 full and 56/87 high products; phenolic thione and thiol-bearing variants also occur. These are chemistry concerns independent of their recorded scores.
Greater aromatic concentration is accompanied by a narrow high-score scaffold set. This is an association under the observed adaptive paths, not attribution to the allocation component.
missing_features: The Child leaders underrepresent the partially saturated, additional-ring and aliphatic-amine variants present in the published Parent high-score set. These chemistries exist elsewhere in the Child output, so this is a local sampling/retention gap, not an impossible edit class.
Many low-score products lose the connected N-heterocycle/aryl architecture entirely or duplicate it into oversized structures rather than preserving a balanced medium-sized product.
No stereochemically specified series or clean, stable alternative to recurrent N-fluorination is demonstrated; the trajectory alone cannot assign the residual score gap to either feature.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 0 evaluation 291 scores 0.49121109476346025 and seed 1 evaluation 265 scores 0.48729853043351984. The 56-heavy-atom repeated bicyclic-core molecule at seed 1 evaluation 67 scores 3.8903446854125574e-43, while the small methyl-dihydroxybenzene at seed 2 evaluation 295 scores 1.9976511210604495e-07. The high Child 87 have 23 to 28 heavy atoms, all with carbonyl groups, versus the low decile median of three heavy atoms. The observed gradient therefore favors a moderate connected heterocyclic/aryl architecture and rejects both severe fragmentation and large repeated cores. The paired Parent high decile is less aromatic and more saturated: mean aromatic atoms 10.586 versus Child 14.931, mean sp3-carbon fraction 0.312 versus 0.203, and mean ring count 3.966 versus 3.057. Parent best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813; Child bests are 0.49121109476346025, 0.48729853043351984 and 0.38761312583727836. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-294ad2ffe1d4, all accepted Search optimizer records on seeds 0/1/2: 1,149/4,350 contain N-halogen bonds, versus 888/4,350 in matched n-cf8d309c06de. One compact aromatic/carboxamide family has 85/87 N-halogenated high-score members and explicit N-Br, N-Cl and N-F analogues with equal score 0.4484138510190879. This is an output association under the retained graph generator, not an attribution of chemical quality to the changed allocation rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted high-score families do not reliably distinguish ordinary carbon halogenation from potentially reactive heteroatom halogenation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs atom-environment-aware access to halogen and other reactive-group edits, and viable nonreactive alternatives at the same attachment sites. Treat N/O-halogen bond formation as chemically distinct from C-halogen substitution; test any general reactivity-aware generation rule on actual current-session feedback rather than assuming a universal score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-294ad2ffe1d4, the complete accepted Search panel: the digest stereocentre text rate is zero in every task, and 2,579/4,350 products have RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres while none has an assigned tetrahedral centre. Two high-score sets each have unassigned centres in all 87 members. Formal charge text is also absent, but many products carry unacylated aliphatic amines; absence of charge notation is not absence of potentially ionisable chemistry. No stereochemical or protonation counterfactual was evaluated.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not express defined stereochemical alternatives even when the generated skeletons have tetrahedral stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator that aims to search defined three-dimensional molecules needs to preserve and construct stereochemical assignments where a graph supports them, with duplicate identity handled consistently. Protonation-state handling is a separate chemical capability that would require its own evidence; neither addition is claimed to improve score on the present record.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-294ad2ffe1d4 under all matched Search sessions: 228/4,350 products contain at most six heavy atoms, versus 98/4,350 for n-cf8d309c06de; 70 such Child products occur at late ordinals 146..290 versus 36 Parent products. All five lowest-score deciles contain tiny fragments, whereas every highest-score decile starts above twenty heavy atoms. One family spends 117 full and 46 late purchases on tiny products. At the other extreme, repeated-core products of 41, 56, 62, 92 and 115 heavy atoms are visibly below their respective compact leaders. This comparison is conditional on the observed initial panel.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently retain a useful molecular size and connected functional architecture when producing novel graphs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic edit construction needs ways to preserve or repair connected source-relative molecular architecture after severe deletion or whole-core concatenation, while allowing legitimate small products to remain testable. The evidence supports examining size-conditioned generation and repair, not imposing one benchmark-specific target size or using a hidden objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-294ad2ffe1d4, complete accepted Search output: 44 products contain a perceived ring of at most four wholly aromatic atoms; the largest observed product has 115 heavy atoms and sixteen perceived rings. High examples also include six-ring chlorinated O/S polycycles with aminal centres and C=C=N, plus a nine-membered-ring aromatic/lactam assembly. The Parent contains related topology concerns; these counts and examples are structural observations, not proof that every flagged molecule is impossible.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid ring novelty is not accompanied by demonstrated geometric or synthetic practicality in the emitted structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction should make chemically interpretable size, fusion, bridge and stereochemical alternatives available while evaluating basic geometry or route plausibility independently of valence acceptance. A generic feasibility-aware proposal capability would address the observed gap; score effects and the contribution of any particular constraint remain unmeasured.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-294ad2ffe1d4 versus matched n-cf8d309c06de, all Search seeds: one high-score set has 10 Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 21, mean ring count 3.057 versus 3.966, sp3-carbon fraction 0.203 versus 0.312, and no unacylated aliphatic-amine proxy versus 45/87 Parent members. Another family has tied N-halogen analogues despite distinct SMILES. This is not a global collapse: other Child high-score sets contain 20, 44, 43 and 47 scaffolds, and saturated amine structures are abundant elsewhere. The contrast is conditioned on actual adaptive trajectories, not a counterfactual attribution to a component.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some productive scaffold families remain dominated by peripheral substitutions while compact alternative ring and linker chemistries are underrepresented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs reliable access to multiple compact skeletal families, including alternate saturation patterns and nitrogen-containing ring/linker arrangements, alongside peripheral decoration. Preserve the distinction between chemical family access and simple SMILES novelty, and let current-session scores determine where those alternatives are useful rather than installing an objective-specific answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-294ad2ffe1d4, the complete accepted Search panel: 168 products have O-O bonds and 34 have the audit N=O nitroso motif. A high-scoring cyclic-carbonyl series includes an N-nitroso analogue at 0.24679583573735037 near its N-methyl leader at 0.2512109625337072. The digest separately records explicit C=C=N and N=C=O products in a polycyclic family. These examples establish chemical liabilities in actual output, not measured toxicity or experimentally proven instability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not reliably separate synthetically ordinary polar groups from reactive substitutes that retain a favorable recorded score.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general proposal vocabulary should represent stable polar-linker alternatives and identify the local reactivity class created by each edit. Reactivity awareness must stay separate from objective scoring: the observed score tolerances justify testing better chemical construction, but do not justify declaring every flagged functional group forbidden or claiming a score improvement without evidence.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
